answer: A stake-backed reputation ledger makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if peers catch it copying identities or faking work. Newcomers cannot simply wander in with a fresh face and harvest trust, because trust accrues only through verified, paid history. Honest behavior is crystal clear on the ledger, while a fake cluster stands out as a mirage — an oasis that vanishes the moment anyone checks the stake behind it.
